diagnostic_evidence.quote: We leave it as an exercise for the reader to prove the following property.
Our next step is to show that $Y_{\tau} y_{\tau} = \frac{1}{n} y_{\tau}$
where $e_0$ is an arbitrary edge of $\tau$.
Let us denote $e_0$'s vertices by $l$ and $r$ and treat them as the terminals.
where the positive sign corresponds to $e$ oriented from $l$ to $r$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the theorem checks the identity $(TY_\tau y_\tau)(e_0)=\frac{T}{n}y_\tau(e_0)$ one row at a time. For each row, the coefficient vector $y_\tau$ is recomputed with the endpoints of that $e_0$ as terminals, and edges are reoriented WLOG accordingly. The values of $\psi$, the decomposition chains and the signs (orientation relative to $l\to r$) all depend on $e_0$. To conclude that one vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $1/n$, the vectors obtained for different $e_0$ must be proportional, possibly with negative factors. That is exactly prop:added-1, which receives no proof, and the theorem's proof never invokes it. The required argument is not a verbatim copy of the proof of prw. It needs $\psi(G\setminus\Gamma)=-\psi(\Gamma)$, which holds because exactly one of $\tau\cap\Gamma$ and $\tau\cap(G\setminus\Gamma)$ joins the shared terminals. It also needs a parity check: the number of complemented factors is odd or even according to whether $e,e'$ separate at a serial or a parallel node, and this sign must match the change of relative st-orientation.

failure_location.quote: Graph-tree-induced edge coefficients are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove prop:added-1 by adapting the re-rooting argument of prw. Use $\psi(G\setminus\Gamma)=-\psi(\Gamma)$ in place of $\phi(x)=\phi(n-x)$, and track the resulting $(-1)^m$ against the change of st-orientation in the serial-meet and parallel-meet cases. Then cite prw and prop:added-1 explicitly in the theorem's proof to identify the row-wise vectors up to a common factor.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the eigenvalue $1/n$ of every spanning-tree submatrix is not established, because each row identity refers to a different vector. The main theorem and the sharpness corollary therefore rest on an unproved claim.
issues.title: Terminal-invariance of (G,tau)-induced coefficients is unproved, yet the main proof silently depends on it
issues.why_classification: The statement appears true (it checks in small cases) and can be proved with a contained re-rooting and sign-parity argument. No new proof architecture is needed, but the step is a nontrivial missing lemma, not routine algebra.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: resulted in their formal description as the star spaces of all nontrivial 2-connected series-parallel graphs
deviates from all the coordinate $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathds{R}^n$ by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$
Having carried out our experiments for all $1 \leq k < n \leq 9$
still leaves more questions than answers

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a description of the class of subspaces with deviation at least $\arccos(1/\sqrt n)$, and a formal description of the extremal subspaces as weighted 2-sp star spaces. The only formal result is one inclusion: each weighted 2-sp star space lies in the class. Nothing proves the converse, the finiteness of the class, or that non-isomorphic series-parallel matroids give inequivalent subspaces. The identification rests on numerical counts for $n\le 9$ matching an OEIS entry.

failure_location.quote: we describe the class of subspaces deviating from all the coordinate ones by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the contribution as exhibiting an explicit family of subspaces in the class, and hence sharpness of the conjectured bound. Present the claim that this family exhausts the extremal subspaces as a conjecture supported by the computations for $n\le 9$.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are told a characterization was obtained, but only an explicit family inside the class, with the resulting sharpness of the hypothesized bound, is established.
issues.title: Abstract and introduction claim a description of the whole class; only membership of the 2-sp family is proved
issues.why_classification: The fix is a rewording, but it necessarily withdraws the advertised characterization. The formal theorem itself is unaffected.
